test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the difference between a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 30% and 5% on a bill of ₹10,00,000?
solution:
**Given:**

Bill amount = Rs 10,00,000

Discount = 35%

Successive discounts = 30% and 5%

**Concept Used:**

Amount = Bill Amount – Discount

**Calculation:**

Amount after single discount = 1000000 – 35% of 1000000

Amount after single discount = 1000000-(35)/(100)× 1000000=1000000-350000=6,50,000 Rs

Amount after successive discount of 30% = 1000000 – 30% of 1000000

Amount after successive discount of 30% = 1000000-(30)/(100)× 1000000=7,00,000 Rs

Amount after a second successive discount of 5% = 700000 – 5% of 700000

Amount after a second successive discount of 5% = 700000-(5)/(100)× 700000=6,65,000 Rs

Difference between single and successive discounts = 665000 – 650000 = Rs 15,000

**Hence, the difference between a single discount and successive discount is of Rs 15,000**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Concept used:**

When two successive discounts X% and Y% are given,

Equivalent discount = (X + Y - XY/100)%

**Calculation:**

Amount after single discount of 35% = 1000000 - (35)/(100) × 1000000

= 1000000 - 350000

= Rs.650,000

Equivalent discount of two successive discount of 30% and 5% -

= [30 + 5 - (30 × 5)/100]

= 33.5%

Amount after equivalent discount = 1000000(1 - 33.5/100)

= 1000000 × 0.665

= Rs.665,000

∴ Difference between them = 665,000 - 650000 = Rs.15000

∴ **Required difference is Rs.15000.**
